chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Asha'ari, with his chain of narrators mentioned in his compilation, which he ascribed to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he said: The defrauded is the one who is defrauded of his age, hour after hour.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be defrauded in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this definition of 'al-maghbun' (the defrauded) to shift the focus from material transaction to spiritual accounting, emphasizing that true loss is the gradual erosion of one's lifespan through heedlessness. This concept aligns with the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (consciousness of God) and the urgency of *faraagh* (utilizing time for worship) before death. It serves as a profound ethical reminder that every moment spent in neglect is a direct theft from one's own eternal benefit.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Yahya ibn Imran al-Asha’ari, with his chain of narrators that is mentioned in his compilation, which he ascribed to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,
that he said: The defrauded is the one who is defrauded of his age, hour after hour.
